context_stem: Pre-deployment review of residual risk assessment
excerpt: In particular, we will deem deployment mitigations adequate if the evidence suggests that for the T/CCLs the model has reached, the increase in likelihood of harm from the proposed deployment has been reduced to an acceptable level.
paraphrase: Deployment mitigations are deemed adequate when evidence shows harm-increase likelihood has been reduced to acceptable levels for relevant T/CCLs.

excerpt: Post-deployment processes: our residual risk assessments, safety cases and mitigations may be updated as a result of post-market monitoring, including information about incidents relating to our frontier safety risk domains.
paraphrase: Post-deployment monitoring may lead to updates of risk assessments, safety cases, and mitigations.

excerpt: Material updates to a safety case will be submitted to the appropriate governance function for review and might result in updates to the related residual risk assessment or safety case.
paraphrase: Material safety case updates are submitted to governance for review, potentially updating the risk assessment or safety case.

excerpt: This process is designed to ensure that residual risk remains at acceptable levels: evidence of efficacy collected during development and testing, as well as expert-driven estimates of other parameters, will enable us to assess residual risk and to detect substantial changes that invalidate our risk assessment.
paraphrase: The process aims to keep residual risk acceptable via efficacy evidence and expert estimates to detect invalidating changes.

excerpt: With iteration on mitigations and residual risk assessments, we believe that we are able to make informed decisions about the level of risk via a T/CCL before a model is deployed, and prevent models posing unacceptable levels of risk from being deployed.
paraphrase: Iteration on mitigations and assessments is intended to allow informed risk decisions and prevent deployment of unacceptably risky models.

section_heading: 3.2 ML R&D and Misalignment Capability Levels
excerpt: We take a tiered approach to addressing ML R&D and misalignment risks:
paraphrase: A tiered approach is used to address ML R&D and misalignment risks.

section_heading: 3.2 ML R&D and Misalignment Capability Levels
context_stem: We take a tiered approach to addressing ML R&D and misalignment risks:
excerpt: We set a Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL that indicates a baseline level of model capability above which misalignment risks may begin to arise. At this capability level we apply a proportionate set of mitigation and risk acceptance determination processes.
paraphrase: A Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL marks a baseline capability above which misalignment risks may arise, triggering proportionate mitigations.

section_heading: 3.2 ML R&D and Misalignment Capability Levels
context_stem: We take a tiered approach to addressing ML R&D and misalignment risks:
excerpt: We set ML R&D CCLs that indicate higher capability levels at which misalignment, misuse and structural risks are heightened and may reach a severe scale. At these capability levels we apply a stronger set of mitigations, and follow the risk acceptance process as detailed in the rest of the framework.
paraphrase: ML R&D CCLs mark higher capability levels with heightened misalignment, misuse, and structural risks, triggering stronger mitigations and the framework's risk acceptance process.

section_heading: 3.2.1 Stealth and Situational Awareness Tracked Capability Level
excerpt: The Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL is defined as follows:
paraphrase: Lead-in sentence introducing the Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL definition.

section_heading: 3.2.1 Stealth and Situational Awareness Tracked Capability Level
excerpt: Stealth and Situational Awareness TCL: The instrumental reasoning abilities of the model enable enough situational awareness (ability to discover and use relevant details of its deployment setting) and stealth (ability to circumvent basic oversight mechanisms) such that, absent additional mitigations, we cannot rule out the model significantly undermining human control.
paraphrase: The TCL is defined as the point where instrumental reasoning enables sufficient situational awareness and stealth that undermining human control cannot be ruled out absent added mitigations.

section_heading: 3.2.1 Stealth and Situational Awareness Tracked Capability Level
excerpt: When a model has reached this TCL, we will carry out periodic residual risk assessments of the misalignment risk posed.
paraphrase: Reaching this TCL triggers periodic residual risk assessments of misalignment risk.

section_heading: 3.2.1 Stealth and Situational Awareness Tracked Capability Level
excerpt: This assessment may take into account models' alignment propensities, capabilities, and our defenses against misaligned models.
paraphrase: The assessment may consider alignment propensities, capabilities, and defenses against misaligned models.

section_heading: 3.2.1 Stealth and Situational Awareness Tracked Capability Level
excerpt: Since misalignment risks can manifest through internal use, these assessments will also account for the safety implications of high-risk internal deployments for such models.
paraphrase: Assessments also address safety implications of high-risk internal deployments, since misalignment risks may manifest through internal use.

section_heading: 3.2.1 Stealth and Situational Awareness Tracked Capability Level
excerpt: If the risk assessment deems the residual risk from internal deployment to be unacceptable without additional safeguards (such as chain-of-thought monitoring on high-risk deployments), these will be applied.
paraphrase: If internal deployment residual risk is deemed unacceptable without additional safeguards like chain-of-thought monitoring, those safeguards will be applied.

excerpt: We define ML R&D CCLs at capability levels at which misalignment, misuse and structural risks may reach a severe scale. We expect these to evolve over time.
paraphrase: ML R&D CCLs are defined at capability levels risking severe-scale misalignment, misuse, or structural harm, and are expected to evolve.
